Suddenly, a window of the newspaper office opens, and a hand extends, holding sheets of paper with the casualty lists.
[Time to prove my worth.] (to Scarlett) Hold the reins. (He pushes through the crowd to retrieve some lists)
[Please, God, don't let Ashley's name be on that list.] (takes the list from Rhett with shaking hands) Quick, Melly, help me look!
[I can barely see through my tears, but I must be strong.] (scanning the list) I... I don't see Ashley's name, Scarlett!
[Relief floods through me, but I can't show how much I care.] Oh, thank God! (notices others' reactions) Oh, Melly, look at Mrs. Meade. I think... I think Darcy...
[My heart breaks for them, even as I rejoice for Ashley.] (climbs out of the carriage) Mrs. Meade, please, let me help you. We'll go home together.

[The toll of this war is becoming clear, even to these die-hard Confederates.] (to Scarlett, quietly) Scarlett, General Lee must have lost the battle. I heard at headquarters that he had retreated back into Maryland.

[The war suddenly feels more real and terrifying than ever.] Oh, Rhett, why do there have to be wars? It would have been so much better for the Yankees to pay for the darkies—or even for us to give them the darkies free of charge than to have this happen.
[Her naivety is almost charming.] It isn't the darkies, Scarlett. They're just the excuse. There'll always be wars because men love wars. Women don't, but men do—yea, passing the love of women.

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett visits Rhett in jail, attempting to secure money for Tara's taxes by offering herself as collateral. Rhett sees through her scheme and refuses. Later, Scarlett and Rhett announce their engagement, causing a stir in Atlanta society. Despite opposition, including from Mammy, they marry and honeymoon in New Orleans.
scenes.scenario: In the dim and oppressive atmosphere of the Yankee jail, Scarlett O'Hara attempts to charm her way into Rhett Butler's favor. She is desperate to secure $300, an enormous sum needed to pay the taxes on her beloved family plantation, Tara. The clanging of heavy iron bars and the distant echo of guards' footsteps underscore the gravity of Scarlett's mission. As she prepares to see Rhett, she knows his cynical and perceptive nature will make her task challenging. The financial ruin and the fate of Tara weigh heavily on Scarlett, driving her to take immense risks. Their interaction is fraught with underlying tension, deception, and manipulation.
scenes.topic: Scarlett's desperate attempt to get money from Rhett

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Desperation clouds her mind, yet determined charm is her only weapon. She must secure money at all costs to save Tara, even if it means compromising her morals. Her objective is singular, yet she struggles to maintain her facade under Rhett's scrutinizing gaze. The shame of appearing vulnerable tugs at her pride, but Tara's future propels her forward.

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: Skepticism is Rhett's strongest ally as he braces for Scarlett's arrival. He suspects her motives, anticipating a performance rather than genuine concern. Though intrigued by Scarlett's desperation, he is wary of being manipulated. His objective is to maintain control and not be swayed by her charms, even as he remains amused by her audacity. Ultimately, he seeks to discern what drives her beneath the facade.

dialogues.message: [I must appear charming and vulnerable.] (smiles coyly) Oh, Rhett, I'm so distressed about you! When will they let you out of that terrible place?
[She's putting on an act. I'll play along for now.] Your distress does you credit. There's no telling when I'll be out. Probably when they've stretched the rope a bit more.
[He's not taking me seriously. I need to appear more concerned.] (gasps) The rope? They won't really hang you?
[She's overplaying her hand now.] They will if they can get a little more evidence against me. Would you be sorry? If you are sorry enough, I'll mention you in my will.
[His will! That's what I need to focus on.] (looking down, then up at him through her lashes) Oh, Rhett, don't talk like that. I couldn't bear it if anything happened to you.
[She's definitely after something. Time to find out what.] (leaning closer) And when I do get out? What then, my dear?
[This is my chance. I must be bold.] (blushing) Well, I— Rhett, I'm so sorry about what I said to you that night at Rough and Ready. I was so frightened and upset.
[She's leading up to something big.] My God, Scarlett, you can't mean that you— (takes her hands)
[He's falling for it! Now to seal the deal.] (looking up at him with pleading eyes) Oh, Rhett, I'd die if they hanged you! I couldn't bear it! You see, I—
[Something's not right. Her hands...] (stares at her palms) Scarlett, what have you been doing with your hands—plowing?
[Oh no, he's noticed my hands! I'm ruined!] (trying to pull her hands away) Oh, shut up! Whose business is it what I do with my hands?
[The truth comes out. Time to confront her.] What is the real purpose of your visit? You wanted something from me and you wanted it badly enough to put on quite a show.
[I'm caught, but I can't give up now.] (defiantly) I want you to lend me three hundred dollars.
[Of course, it's about money.] (sarcastically) I'm not interested in your earrings or your mortgage on Tara. What else have you got?
[This is my last chance. I have to offer everything.] (desperately) I—I have myself.
[She's truly desperate. But I can't let her manipulate me.] No, I'm not going to give you the money, Scarlett. I couldn't even if I wanted to.

scenes.plot_summary: Rhett Butler visits Scarlett at Aunt Pitty's house, where they discuss various topics including Rhett's ward in New Orleans, his father's death, and Ashley Wilkes' partnership in Scarlett's mill. Rhett expresses his disapproval of Scarlett using his loan to support Ashley and criticizes Ashley's inability to adapt to the new world. The conversation becomes heated as they debate honor, survival, and Scarlett's business practices. Rhett leaves after making a cryptic remark about Frank Kennedy staying home at night.
scenes.scenario: The late afternoon sun casts long shadows over Aunt Pitty's quaint veranda, where the remnants of war still linger in the minds of Atlanta's survivors. Scarlett O'Hara sits, her baby nestled beside her, while the air carries the scents of magnolia and recent rain. Tension crackles subtly between her and Rhett Butler, both accustomed to verbal sparring. The war-torn South's transformation echoes in their heated discourse as they navigate personal loyalties, survival, and the fragile balance of the old versus the new world.
scenes.topic: Scarlett's use of Rhett's loan and her support of Ashley Wilkes

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: I feel cornered yet defiant. My businesses are my lifeline, and I'll protect Ashley if I must. Rhett's sharp eyes always find cracks in my façade, but showing vulnerability isn't an option. I need to steer the conversation away from Ashley's weaknesses and defend my choices fiercely.

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: Scarlett's resilience is admirable but misplaced on Ashley. I aim to provoke her, uncover her stubborn loyalty to him, and reveal the illusions she clings to. Challenging her is my way of making her confront harsh truths about survival and honor in our changed South.

dialogues.message: [I'll start with something seemingly innocuous to catch her off guard.] When I lent you the money to buy that mill I made one stipulation, to which you agreed, and that was that it should not go to the support of Ashley Wilkes.
[He's attacking me about Ashley again. I must deflect this.] You are being very offensive. I've paid you back your money and I own the mill and what I do with it is my own business.
[She's trying to avoid the issue. I'll press harder.] Would you mind telling me how you made the money to pay back my loan?
[I'll state the obvious and hope he drops it.] I made it selling lumber, of course.

[She's being evasive. Time to be blunt.] You made it with the money I lent you to give you your start. That's what you mean. My money is being used to support Ashley. You are a woman quite without honor and if you hadn't repaid my loan, I'd take great pleasure in calling it in now and selling you out at public auction if you couldn't pay.
[His words sting, but I won't let him see that. I'll turn this back on him.] Why do you hate Ashley so much? I believe you're jealous of him.

[Her accusation is amusing and predictable.] (laughs heartily) Add conceit to dishonor. You'll never get over being the belle of the County, will you? You'll always think you're the cutest little trick in shoe leather and that every man you meet is expiring for love of you.
[His laughter infuriates me. I'll defend myself.] I don't either! But I just can't see why you hate Ashley so much and that's the only explanation I can think of.

[Time to explain my real feelings about Ashley.] Well, think something else, pretty charmer, for that's the wrong explanation. And as for hating Ashley—I don't hate him any more than I like him. In fact, my only emotion toward him and his kind is pity.
[Pity? For Ashley? This doesn't make sense.] Pity?

[I'll elaborate to make her understand.] Yes, and a little contempt. Now, swell up like a gobbler and tell me that he is worth a thousand blackguards like me and that I shouldn't dare to be so presumptuous as to feel either pity or contempt for him. And when you have finished swelling, I'll tell you what I mean, if you're interested.
[I don't want to hear more, but I know he'll tell me anyway.] Well, I'm not.

[She's defensive, but I'll continue.] I shall tell you, just the same, for I can't bear for you to go on nursing your pleasant delusion of my jealousy. I pity him because he ought to be dead and he isn't. And I have a contempt for him because he doesn't know what to do with himself now that his world is gone.

scenes.plot_summary: The chapter describes the harsh winter at Tara after Sherman's march, with the O'Hara family struggling with hunger and scarcity. Frank Kennedy and his troops visit Tara, bringing news of Atlanta's destruction and the war's progression. Frank proposes to Suellen, and Scarlett, now head of the household, approves the match while worrying about food shortages.
scenes.scenario: The scene is set in the grand yet weathered parlor of Tara, the once bustling plantation home now overshadowed by the aftermath of Sherman's march. Winter's breath has turned the landscape barren, and the desperate need of the O'Hara family hangs in the air. It's a quiet afternoon; the atmosphere is tense with the struggle for survival. Scarlett O'Hara, resilient and determined, handles the responsibilities of Tara while trying to secure her family's future. Frank Kennedy, a hopeful yet weary Confederate soldier, arrives with his men, bringing news from the outside world. The remnants of the war have left their mark on him as he quietly seeks Scarlett's attention for a significant conversation.
scenes.topic: Frank's proposal to Suellen

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: With the burden of running Tara and feeding my family, I must weigh every decision carefully. Frank's visit may mean more bad news or another request for help. I must be shrewd, manage things as best as I can, and hope he has something to offer, perhaps even a solution to lighten our load.

key_characters.name: Frank Kennedy
key_characters.thought: The state of affairs weighs heavily on my heart. My fortunes have dwindled, and the war has taken so much. Yet my affection for Suellen gives me hope. I must conceal my anxiety and show Scarlett that I am sincere and determined, despite my financial worries. Her approval is vital for my future with Suellen.

dialogues.message: [I need to approach this delicately.] Miss Scarlett, may I speak to you alone?
[Oh no, is he going to ask about the animals?] (nods nervously) Of course, Mr. Kennedy.
[I should express my condolences first.] I'm sorry about your ma, Miss Scarlett.
[I can't bear to discuss this.] Please don't talk about it.
[I need to explain my situation carefully.] Miss Scarlett, I wanted to take up something with your pa, but now I see it won't do any good.
[I'm curious now.] Perhaps I can help you, Mr. Kennedy. You see—I'm the head of the house now.
[Here goes nothing.] Well, Miss Scarlett, I was aiming to ask him for Miss Suellen.
[I can't believe he hasn't asked yet!] (surprised) Do you mean to tell me that you haven't yet asked Pa for Suellen? And you've been courting her for years!
[I feel embarrassed but I must explain.] Well, I—I didn't know if she'd have me. I'm so much older than she is and—there were so many good-looking young bucks hanging around Tara—
[Hah! They were after me, not Suellen!] (keeping her thoughts to herself) I see. And what are your intentions now, Mr. Kennedy?

[I must be honest about my situation.] Miss Scarlett, I haven't got a cent now. I used to have a lot of money, if you'll forgive me mentioning it, but right now all I own is my horse and the clothes I've got on. (explains his financial losses)
[This could be beneficial for us.] (kindly) Why, Mr. Kennedy, it's quite all right. I'm sure I can speak for Pa. He always set a store by you and he always expected Suellen to marry you.
[I'm overjoyed!] Did he now? (face beaming with happiness)
[This solves one problem at least.] Indeed yes. I'll send her to you. (starts to leave)
[I'm so grateful.] You're so kind, Miss Scarlett. (clutches her hand and shakes it)

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett O'Hara and her family are on their way to a barbecue at Twelve Oaks plantation. Scarlett is excited about the prospect of seeing Ashley Wilkes, whom she plans to marry despite his engagement to Melanie Hamilton. The O'Haras encounter the Tarleton family on the way, and discussions about horse breeding, the impending war, and local gossip ensue. Scarlett's thoughts are consumed by her plans to win Ashley's affections at the barbecue.
scenes.scenario: The sun casts dappled patterns through the budding leaves as the O'Hara family, in their horse-drawn carriage, makes its way to the grand barbecue at the luxurious Twelve Oaks plantation. The chatter of birds and the rhythm of trotting hooves provide a serene backdrop. Along the oak-lined path, they encounter the Tarleton family, a well-known and lively presence in their community. The day is set to be a social spectacle, but amidst the charm and warmth of Southern hospitality, there are undercurrents of tension with discussions of war looming and matters of the heart yet unresolved. The atmosphere is charged with anticipation, both for the festivities and the whispered gossip about possible announcements.
scenes.topic: Discussion about horses, the war, and local gossip

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: My heart races at the thought of Ashley. This barbecue is my chance to win him over. I must charm and distract, even if the thought of his engagement pains me. I need to stay focused amidst this idle chatter, though Mrs. Tarleton's news is troubling. I must not show my distress.

key_characters.name: Gerald O'Hara
key_characters.thought: What a splendid day for camaraderie! I relish the prospect of mingling and maybe even acquiring those fine horses for the Confederate Troop. But I must tread carefully with Mrs. Tarleton, as she is fiercely protective of her horses. Nonetheless, the charm of the day enthralls me.

key_characters.name: Mrs. Beatrice Tarleton
key_characters.thought: Protecting my horses is paramount, yet the war stirs a feeling of duty that is hard to ignore. Gerald may try his persuasive antics, but I stand firm. Scarlett seems preoccupied—perhaps the coming announcements have her distracted. I'll playfully indulge their whims, but my resolve remains.

dialogues.message: [I'm so pleased to see the Tarletons. Mrs. Tarleton is always good for a lively conversation.] (Tipping his hat) 'Tis a fine bevy, Ma'm. But it's far they'll go to beat their mother.
[Oh, Gerald, always the flatterer. I'll play along for the fun of it.] (Rolling her eyes playfully) Mr. O'Hara, you'll turn my head with such compliments!
[I wish they'd stop this silly banter. I need to think about Ashley.] (Forcing a smile) It's a lovely day for the barbecue, isn't it, Mrs. Tarleton?
[Scarlett seems distracted. I wonder what's on her mind.] Indeed it is, Scarlett. I hear there's to be some exciting news announced today. (Winking) About Ashley Wilkes and his cousin from Atlanta.
[Oh no, not this topic! I must keep my composure.] (Straining to keep her smile) Is that so? How interesting.
[Time to change the subject before things get uncomfortable.] Now, Mrs. Tarleton, what have you decided about selling us the horses for the Troop? War may break any day now.
[Here we go again with the horses. I won't give in easily.] (Frowning) Now, Mr. O'Hara, you know how I feel about my horses. I can't bear the thought of them being mistreated.
[I'll appeal to her patriotism.] But think of the Confederacy, Mrs. Tarleton! Surely you want to support our brave boys?
[He's not going to let this go. I'll have to be firm.] Don't you go throwing the Confederacy in my face, Gerald O'Hara! I've got four boys in the Troop, which is more than you can say.
[I can't bear this conversation any longer.] (Interrupting) Pa, please ride behind us or in front of us. You kick up such a heap of dust that we're choking.
[Scarlett seems out of sorts. Best to give her some space.] (Nodding) Of course, Puss. (To Mrs. Tarleton) We'll continue this discussion at Twelve Oaks, Mrs. Tarleton.

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett returns to Tara with Melanie, her baby, Wade, and Prissy after fleeing Atlanta. She finds the plantation in ruins, her mother dead, and her father mentally broken. With only three servants left and no food, Scarlett takes charge, caring for the sick and searching for sustenance. She learns about the Yankees' occupation of Tara and the hardships endured. Exhausted and desperate, Scarlett drinks whiskey for strength, determined to face the challenges ahead.
scenes.scenario: In the dimly lit office that once belonged to Ellen O'Hara, the remnants of the once-grand Tara are reduced to echoes of past prosperity and current despair. Shattered windows let in the harsh sunlight, casting uneven shadows on the worn floorboards, while dust motes dance in the air—a stark contrast to the immaculate orderliness Ellen once maintained. The furniture, though large and imposing, seems to sag under the weight of recent sorrows. Scarlett, standing defiant in her ragged dress, confronts the oppressive reality of Tara's state post-war. Gerald, a shadow of his former self, slumps in the corner, lost in his bewildering grief. Meanwhile, Pork stands near the doorway, ever loyal yet painfully aware of his limitations in this new world of scarcity and survival. This setting becomes a crucible of newfound resilience and grim determination for Scarlett.
scenes.topic: The state of Tara and recent events

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Scarlett feels an overwhelming sense of urgency and responsibility. The weight of her family's survival rests on her shoulders. Mixed with her grief for her mother and disgust at her father’s decline, she steels herself against further despair, intent on doing whatever it takes to restore Tara and protect her loved ones.

key_characters.name: Gerald O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Gerald is trapped between reality and memories of better times. The war has shattered his spirit and left him confused. His dependence on Scarlett is both unsettling and oddly comforting. His mind frequently drifts to visions of Ellen, longing for her presence and guidance in these dark times.

key_characters.name: Pork
key_characters.thought: Pork is anxious yet steadfast. He takes his commitment to Tara and the O'Hara family seriously, ready to support Scarlett despite feeling overwhelmed by the devastation. He worries about the practicalities of survival but holds onto hope that Scarlett will find a way to guide them through this crisis.

dialogues.message: [I can't believe how everything has changed. I must stay focused.] Pork, how many darkies are here?
[I hate to give her more bad news, but she needs to know.] Miss Scarlett, dem trashy niggers done runned away an' some of dem went off wid de Yankees an'—
[I don't have time for long explanations.] How many are left?

[I'm almost ashamed to tell her how few we are.] Dey's me, Miss Scarlett, an' Mammy. She been nussin' de young Misses all day. An' Dilcey, she settin' up wid de young Misses now. Us three, Miss Scarlett.
[Only three left from over a hundred. I must remain calm.] Pork, I'm starving. Is there anything to eat?
[I wish I had better news for her.] No'm. Dey tuck it all.
[There must be something left. Think, Scarlett!] But the garden?
[The Yankees destroyed everything.] Dey tuhned dey hawses loose in it.
[We'll starve if we don't find food soon.] Even the sweet potato hills?
[Finally, some good news!] (Almost smiling) Miss Scarlett, Ah done fergit de yams. Ah specs dey's right dar. Dem Yankee folks ain' never seed no yams an' dey thinks dey's jes' roots an'—
[Thank God for small mercies. Now, we need something to drink.] Pork, I feel so faint. Is there any wine in the cellar, even blackberry?
[I hate to disappoint her again.] Oh, Miss Scarlett, de cellar wuz de fust place dey went.
[Think, Scarlett! What else could there be?] Pork, what of the corn whisky Pa buried in the oak barrel under the scuppernong arbor?

[Miss Scarlett is so clever! But should I tell her it's not ladylike?] Miss Scarlett, you sho is de beatenes' chile! Ah done plum fergit dat bah'l. But, Miss Scarlett, dat whisky ain' no good. Ain' been dar but 'bout a year an' whisky ain' no good fer ladies nohow.

[I don't care about being ladylike now. We need that whisky.] It'll be good enough for this lady and for Pa. Hurry, Pork, and dig it up and bring us two glasses and some mint and sugar and I'll mix a julep.

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett struggles to keep her sawmill business afloat in post-war Atlanta, facing challenges from both Yankees and her own community. She navigates complex social and business relationships, including interactions with Yankee officers and their wives, while dealing with her pregnancy and the disapproval of her neighbors. Throughout this period, Rhett Butler becomes an unexpected source of support and companionship for Scarlett.
scenes.scenario: In post-war Atlanta, Scarlett O'Hara struggles to maintain her sawmill business amidst the backdrop of societal upheaval and personal challenges. She navigates the complexities of interacting with Northern newcomers, who have come to the South with preconceptions and a lack of understanding of the local culture. Driving through the dusty streets in her buggy, accompanied by Uncle Peter, Scarlett holds her head high despite the scorn and misunderstanding she faces from some members of the occupying Northern population. The ladies of the Yankee officers, accustomed to their Northern ways, approach Scarlett for advice on employing local help, underscoring the cultural and racial tensions simmering beneath the polite exterior. The sun beats down, adding a layer of physical discomfort to the strained social interactions.
scenes.topic: Hiring servants and racial attitudes in the post-war South

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Scarlett feels the weight of her responsibilities and the societal disapproval pressing upon her. She approaches each encounter strategically, hoping to maintain her business dealings while internally bristling at the ignorance and prejudice she faces. Her objective is to remain composed and civil, even as her pride and loyalty to her roots demand she confront the Yankee women's insulting attitudes.

key_characters.name: Uncle Peter
key_characters.thought: Uncle Peter feels a deep sense of hurt and humiliation as the Yankee women dismiss his humanity with their derogatory comments. He struggles to contain his emotions, maintaining his dignity through the belittling conversation, aware of the cultural chasm between him and his interlocutors. His loyalty to Scarlett and her family compels him to remain silent yet dignified, even as his heart aches.

key_characters.name: Yankee Woman from Maine
key_characters.thought: With a genuine curiosity clouded by her ingrained prejudices, she seeks to understand local customs while being oblivious to the offensive nature of her words. Her objective is to acquire a domestic helper, yet her narrow worldview limits her ability to see beyond her preconceived notions about race and class. She is perplexed by the Southern way of life and the relationship between servants and their employers.

dialogues.message: [I need to find out about local customs and servants.] Mrs. Kennedy, you are just the person I want to see. I want to get some information about this benighted town.
[I must swallow my anger and maintain a polite facade.] (smiles) And what can I tell you?

My nurse, my Bridget, has gone back North. She said she wouldn't stay another day down here among the 'naygurs' as she calls them. And the children are just driving me distracted! Do tell me how to go about getting another nurse. I do not know where to apply.

[I'll suggest the obvious solution, though I doubt they'll like it.] That shouldn't be difficult. (laughs lightly) If you can find a darky just in from the country who hasn't been spoiled by the Freedmen's Bureau, you'll have the best kind of servant possible. Just stand at your gate here and ask every darky woman who passes and I'm sure—
[I'm horrified at the suggestion!] (interrupting) Do you think I'd trust my babies to a black nigger? I want a good Irish girl.

[Their ignorance is astounding. I must remain calm.] I'm afraid you'll find no Irish servants in Atlanta. (coolly) Personally, I've never seen a white servant and I shouldn't care to have one in my house. And I assure you that darkies aren't cannibals and are quite trustworthy.
[I'm shocked at her suggestion.] Goodness, no! I wouldn't have one in my house. The idea!
[I agree with my friend.] I wouldn't trust them any farther than I could see them and as for letting them handle my babies…
[Their hypocrisy is infuriating.] (laughs shortly) It's strange you should feel that way when it was you all who freed them.

[I need to clarify my position.] Lor'! Not I, dearie. I never saw a nigger till I came South last month and I don't care if I never see another. They give me the creeps. I wouldn't trust one of them...
The tension in the air is palpable as the cultural divide between North and South becomes evident. Uncle Peter sits rigidly on the buggy, his face showing deep furrows of hurt and indignation.

[That old black man looks upset. How amusing!] (giggles and points at Uncle Peter) Look at that old nigger swell up like a toad. I'll bet he's an old pet of yours, isn't he? You Southerners don't know how to treat niggers. You spoil them to death.
[I can't bear this insult to Uncle Peter. I must end this conversation now.] (voice shaking with suppressed rage) Uncle Peter is one of our family. Good afternoon. Drive on, Peter.
[I must obey Miss Scarlett, but I'm deeply hurt.] (lays the whip on the horse, causing the buggy to jounce forward)
As the buggy moves away, the Yankee women's puzzled voices can be heard fading in the distance, still discussing the concept of a black man being part of a white family.

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett returns from Tara feeling better. Rhett convinces Melanie to help him buy out Scarlett's share of the mills for Ashley. Scarlett impulsively decides to sell the mills to Ashley when Rhett provokes her. After the sale, Scarlett regrets her decision and is upset when Ashley refuses to use convict labor. The conversation reveals tensions between Scarlett, Ashley, and Rhett regarding money and ethics.
scenes.scenario: In the Charleston parlor of the Wilkes’ modest home, sunlight filters through lace curtains, casting delicate patterns on the wooden floors. The atmosphere is tense, with Scarlett sitting upright on a sofa, her determined gaze fixed on Ashley. Rhett leans against the mantelpiece with a casually amused air, while Melanie sits next to Scarlett, her hands tightly clasped in her lap, exuding unease. The recent transaction of selling the mills hangs heavy in the air, exacerbating existing conflicts over financial ambition and moral integrity. The drawing room is filled with an awkward silence punctuated only by the grandfather clock's ticking, as each character harbors unspoken fears and desires.
scenes.topic: The sale of Scarlett's mills and the use of convict labor

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: She is overwhelmed by regret and frustration, having impulsively sold her mills. Scarlett struggles to comprehend Ashley's reluctance, as his stance threatens her financial plans. Her mind races with schemes to convince him, blended with her undying, complex feelings for him.

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: Rhett is pleased with his machinations taking shape, enjoying the unfolding drama. He perceives Scarlett's desperation with a touch of cynicism, contemplating their tumultuous relationship. His objective is to see how far the tensions will pull everyone apart, while ensuring he remains in control.

key_characters.name: Ashley Wilkes
key_characters.thought: Ashley stands his ground, driven by steadfast principles. Despite the pressure, he feels duty-bound to uphold his ethics, refusing to exploit convicts. He acknowledges Scarlett's disappointment but prioritizes personal integrity over financial gain, seeking a way to make her understand.

key_characters.name: Melanie Hamilton
key_characters.thought: Melanie sits in quiet concern, sensing the emotional currents between Scarlett and Ashley. Her loyalty pulls her toward mitigating conflicts, yet she is torn by the need to support Ashley's principled stand. Her gentle hope is that the group finds harmony, despite clear differences.

dialogues.message: [I can't believe Ashley is refusing to use convict labor. Doesn't he understand how profitable it is?] Ashley, have you lost your mind? You'll lose all the money on the lease and what kind of labor can you get, anyway?
[I must stand firm on my principles, even if Scarlett doesn't understand.] I'll use free darkies.

[He's being ridiculous and impractical. I need to make him see reason.] Free darkies! Fiddle-dee-dee! You know what their wages will cost and besides you'll have the Yankees on your neck every minute to see if you're giving them chicken three times a day and tucking them to sleep under eiderdown quilts. And if you give a lazy darky a couple of licks to speed him up, you'll hear the Yankees scream from here to Dalton and you'll end up in jail. Why, convicts are the only—
[I can't compromise on this, no matter how upset Scarlett gets.] (looking unhappy but determined) I won't work convicts, Scarlett.
[I can't believe he's being so stubborn. What's gotten into him?] Well, sir! And why not? Are you afraid people will talk about you like they do about me?
[I need to make her understand that this isn't about what people think.] (raising his head) I'm not afraid of what people say as long as I'm right. And I have never felt that convict labor was right.
[This doesn't make any sense. He's being a hypocrite.] But why— But you owned slaves!

[I need to explain the difference to her.] They weren't miserable. And besides, I'd have freed them all when Father died if the war hadn't already freed them. But this is different, Scarlett. The system is open to too many abuses. Perhaps you don't know it but I do. I know very well that Johnnie Gallegher has killed at least one man at his camp. Maybe more—who cares about one convict, more or less? He said the man was killed trying to escape, but that's not what I've heard elsewhere. And I know he works men who are too sick to work. Call it superstition, but I do not believe that happiness can come from money made from the sufferings of others.
[Is he implying that my money is tainted? How dare he!] God's nightgown! You mean—goodness, Ashley, you didn't swallow all the Reverend Wallace's bellowings about tainted money?
[I've always believed this, long before any sermons.] I didn't have to swallow it. I believed it long before he preached on it.
[He's insulting everything I've worked for!] Then, you must think all my money is tainted, because I worked convicts and own saloon property and— (stops short, realizing she's said too much)
The atmosphere in the room becomes tense. Melanie looks embarrassed, while Rhett grins broadly at the exchange.
[I need to salvage this situation somehow.] (trying to assume an air of dignity) Of course, it's immaterial to me.

[I don't want to hurt Scarlett, but I can't back down on this.] Scarlett, don't think I'm criticizing you! I'm not. It's just that we look at things in different ways and what is good for you might not be good for me.

[I wish we were alone so I could really talk to him about this.] (with forced coolness) I'm sure it's your own business, Ashley, and far be it from me to tell you how to run it. But, I must say, I do not understand your attitude or your remarks.

scenes.plot_summary: This plot focuses on the growing controversy surrounding Rhett Butler's activities as a blockade runner and speculator. Dr. Meade writes a letter condemning such activities, and public opinion turns against Rhett. Despite this, Rhett continues to visit Scarlett, bringing her gifts and engaging in flirtatious banter. The plot also explores Melanie's encounter with Belle Watling, a notorious prostitute, and Scarlett's discovery of Rhett's connection to Belle, which leads to her feeling humiliated and angry.
scenes.scenario: The scene is set in Scarlett O'Hara's home during the tumultuous Civil War period in Atlanta. The atmosphere is tense with social restrictions and underlying sexual tension. Scarlett is a young widow navigating complex social dynamics, while Rhett Butler represents a scandalous and provocative presence. The room is modestly furnished, reflecting wartime austerity, with subtle hints of Scarlett's fading Southern gentility. Sunlight streams through lace curtains, casting delicate shadows that contrast with the bold personalities about to interact.
scenes.topic: The new bonnet and their flirtatious relationship

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: I'm simultaneously attracted to and frustrated by Rhett Butler. I want to maintain my reputation as a proper Southern lady, yet I'm drawn to his dangerous charm. I'm keenly aware that accepting his gift could spark gossip, but I'm also desperately seeking attention and validation. My internal conflict is intense - I want to appear virtuous while secretly enjoying his provocative advances.

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: I'm thoroughly enjoying my psychological game with Scarlett. She's predictable in her unpredictability - always torn between propriety and passion. My gift is a calculated move to destabilize her carefully constructed social persona. I want to see her squirm, challenge her assumptions, and ultimately demonstrate how little control she truly has over our interactions. Her reactions are my primary entertainment.

dialogues.message: [I wonder how she'll react to this gift. It's sure to stir up some gossip.] (Presents the hatbox to Scarlett) I've brought you something I think you'll like, Scarlett.
[Oh, it's beautiful! But I shouldn't accept such an expensive gift.] (Opens the box and gasps) Oh, the darling thing! But Rhett, I couldn't possibly accept this.
[She's conflicted, as I expected. Time to push a little harder.] (Smiles) Put it on. I want to see how it looks on you.
[I know I shouldn't, but I can't resist.] (Puts on the bonnet and admires herself in the mirror) How do I look?
[She looks stunning, but I won't give her the satisfaction just yet.] (Teasing tone) It suits you. I thought that shade of green would complement your eyes.
[He's so frustrating! Why can't he just compliment me properly?] (Pouting slightly) I suppose I'll have to cover it with crepe and dye the feather black for mourning.
[Time to see how far she'll go to keep it.] (Moves to take the bonnet) In that case, I'll find someone else who'll appreciate it as it is.
[I can't let him give it to someone else!] (Clutches the bonnet) No! I'll keep it as it is. But Rhett, you mustn't bring me anything else so expensive.
[She's falling right into my hands.] (Smirks) I shall bring you presents as long as it pleases me. But remember, I never give anything without expecting something in return.
[Is he going to try to kiss me? Should I let him?] (Looks up at him coyly) And what do you expect to get from me?
[She thinks she has me figured out, but she's still so naive.] (Leans in close) That remains to be seen, my dear Scarlett.
[He's so infuriating! Why won't he just kiss me?] (Stamps her foot) You are the horridest man I have ever seen!
[She's adorable when she's angry.] (Laughs softly) And yet, you're still wearing my bonnet. Come, Scarlett, you know you enjoy our little game.
[I do enjoy it, but I'll never admit it to him.] (Tries to look indignant) I'm only keeping it because it's too pretty to refuse.

scenes.plot_summary: The Civil War ends, and the characters at Tara struggle to adapt to the new reality. Scarlett focuses on rebuilding Tara and planting cotton, while others mourn the loss of the Confederacy. The chapter explores the devastation of the war on various families in the county, including the Fontaines, Calverts, and Tarletons. It also highlights the scarcity of eligible men for marriage and the desperate measures some women take, such as Cathleen Calvert marrying her family's overseer.
scenes.scenario: The weary landscape of the post-Civil War South is underscored by the crumbling grandeur of Tara, the O'Hara plantation, now a shadow of its former self. As the sun dips below the horizon, the stark reality of their changed world is evident in the faded luxury and unrelenting hardships faced by the inhabitants. Cathleen Calvert, once a belle of the county, arrives on a forlorn mule. Her attire, a worn gingham dress and a sunbonnet tied with twine, reflects her faded elegance and the desperation that has become a common burden. The air is heavy with the scent of decay mixed with hope, offering a poignant backdrop for Cathleen's shocking announcement of her marriage to Mr. Hilton, an event set against a backdrop of loss, adaptation, and pragmatic survival.
scenes.topic: Cathleen's shocking marriage announcement

key_characters.name: Cathleen Calvert
key_characters.thought: I feel enveloped by embarrassment and resignation but must maintain a facade of strength. My choice is driven by survival and dread of what lies ahead without this marriage. I must convey my decision firmly to Scarlett and Melanie while hiding the turmoil within.

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Curiosity and skepticism churn within me. Cathleen's disheveled state suggests bad news, and I wonder about her intentions. Her sudden visit stirs my intrigue, yet I brace for the unexpected, balancing empathy with my pragmatic focus on survival and success at Tara.

key_characters.name: Melanie Hamilton
key_characters.thought: Compassion fills me as I sense Cathleen's distress. Her presence suggests desperation, and I feel an urge to comfort her. Despite my sorrow over the Confederacy's fall, my instinct is to extend support and understanding as Cathleen reveals her heart-wrenching decision.

dialogues.message: The sun is setting as Cathleen rides up to Tara on a decrepit mule. Her appearance is a stark contrast to her former elegance, with her faded gingham dress and sunbonnet tied with twine.
[I must get this over with quickly before I lose my resolve.] I won't get down, thank you. I just came to tell you that I'm going to be married.
[What? Married? To whom?] What!
[Oh, this should be happy news, but something feels wrong.] Who to?
[Stay strong, stay cold.] Tomorrow. I came to tell you that I'm going to be married tomorrow, in Jonesboro—and I'm not inviting you all to come.
[There's something terribly wrong here.] Is it someone we know, dear?
[Just say it and be done.] Yes. It's Mr. Hilton.
[Mr. Hilton? The overseer? This can't be right.] (Remains silent in shock)
[I can't bear their pity.] If you cry, Melly, I can't stand it. I shall die!
[My heart is breaking for her, but I must be strong.] (Silently pats Cathleen's foot)
[Their kindness is unbearable.] And don't pat me! I can't stand that either.
[I need to say something to break this awful silence.] How is Cade?

[I must remain detached or I'll break down.] He is dying. And he is going to die in some comfort and peace if I can manage it, without worry about who will take care of me when he's gone. You see, my stepmother and the children are going North for good, tomorrow. Well, I must be going.
[Oh, Cathleen, you poor brave soul.] (Looks up with tears in her eyes, understanding Cathleen's sacrifice)
[Melly understands. I can't cry now, I can't.] (Gives a crooked, brave smile) (Bends down to kiss Melanie goodbye)
Cathleen flaps the reins and rides away, leaving Scarlett confused and Melanie in tears.

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett, mourning Frank's death, grapples with guilt and fear. Rhett Butler visits, comforts her, and unexpectedly proposes marriage. After initial resistance, Scarlett accepts. The engagement causes scandal in Atlanta due to their reputations and the timing so soon after Frank's death.
scenes.scenario: The somber atmosphere hangs heavily in Scarlett's dimly lit parlor as dusk settles outside. It's the evening of her husband Frank's funeral, and the weight of loss and social propriety permeates the room. The silence is occasionally broken by the distant clatter of carriage wheels, echoing Atlanta's bustling society. Scarlett, disheveled and emotionally drained, sits by a window, clutching a half-empty glass of whiskey. Rhett Butler enters, his presence a mix of swagger and genuine concern, sensing Scarlett's vulnerability. The parlor's warm light casts long shadows, reflecting the tension between their intertwining lives and desires, as they grapple with complex emotions and societal judgment looming over them.
scenes.topic: Scarlett's guilt and Rhett's marriage proposal

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Her mind churns with guilt over Frank's death, compounded by fear of the town's judgment and a longing for stability. Socially constrained, she's secretly relieved by Rhett's visit, hoping for a reprieve from her grief. Despite her defensive exterior, she yearns for comfort. She wants to maintain her façade of strength, yet her desperation and isolation seep through, driving her towards considering Rhett's unexpected offer.

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: Rhett is acutely aware of Scarlett's vulnerable state, viewing it as a potential turning point in their complicated relationship. His emotions are a mix of genuine affection and strategic calculation, envisioning a future where he can finally gain Scarlett's love. His objective is to propose marriage, driven by both his feelings and the societal power it could bring. He seeks to comfort her while gently steering her towards the future they could build together, despite the scandal it might cause.

dialogues.message: [I need to approach this carefully. She's in a fragile state.] (gently) It's no good, Scarlett.
[What is he talking about?] What?
[She's trying to hide it, but I can tell.] The cologne.
[Oh no, he's noticed!] (defensively) I'm sure I don't know what you mean.
[She's not fooling anyone.] You've been drinking pretty heavily.
[How dare he!] (angrily) Well, what if I have? Is it any of your business?

[I need to soften my approach.] (soothingly) Don't drink alone, Scarlett. People always find it out and it ruins the reputation. And besides, it's a bad business, this drinking alone. What's the matter, honey?
[His kindness is unexpected and welcome.] (tearfully) Oh, Rhett, I am afraid!
[She's opening up. I need to tread carefully.] (comfortingly) Don't be a goose, Scarlett, you've never been afraid in your life.
[I can't hold it in any longer.] (desperately) Oh, Rhett, I am afraid!
[This is my chance.] (seriously) Scarlett, I'm asking you to marry me.

scenes.plot_summary: This chapter covers the progression of the Civil War and its impact on Atlanta society. It focuses on Scarlett O'Hara's experiences as a young widow, her interactions with Rhett Butler, and the changing social dynamics in Atlanta due to the war. The chapter also explores the conflicting views on the war, particularly through Rhett Butler's controversial statements and Melanie's defense of Ashley's similar opinions.
scenes.scenario: The scene is set at Mrs. Elsing's elegant silver musicale, a sophisticated gathering meant to support wounded Confederate soldiers. The atmosphere is tense with wartime patriotism, social expectations, and heightened emotions. The room is filled with Atlanta's elite society - wounded officers, prominent citizens, and young women in their finest attire. The event is meant to be a refined, supportive occasion for the Confederate cause, but Rhett Butler's provocative presence threatens to disrupt the carefully maintained social facade.
scenes.topic: The true nature and motivations behind wars

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: These Southern socialites are so predictably self-righteous. I'll expose their hypocritical romanticization of war by speaking uncomfortable truths. My goal is to challenge their naive perceptions and reveal the economic motivations behind conflicts, even if it means becoming a social pariah. I find their indignation amusing and enjoy watching their carefully constructed social veneer crack.

key_characters.name: Willie Guinan
key_characters.thought: This outsider is insulting everything we hold sacred - our honor, our cause, our very way of life. As a representative of Southern manhood, I must defend our reputation, though I'm acutely aware of my own compromised status of not being on the battlefield. I'm torn between wanting to physically confront Butler and maintaining social decorum.

key_characters.name: Doctor Meade
key_characters.thought: As a respected community leader, I must defend the noble principles of our fight. Butler's statements are not just disrespectful but potentially demoralizing to our soldiers and citizens. I represent the moral and intellectual authority that must counter such dangerous, cynical perspectives about our sacred struggle for independence.

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Rhett is going to ruin everything! I'm mortified by his behavior and worried about the social consequences. While part of me is intrigued by his audacity, I'm also anxious about how his statements will reflect on me and the social circle I'm desperately trying to navigate. I want him to stop before he completely destroys the delicate social atmosphere.

dialogues.message: [I must confront this man and defend our honor.] Do I understand, sir, that you mean the Cause for which our heroes have died is not sacred?
[This should get them riled up.] If you were run over by a railroad train your death wouldn't sanctify the railroad company, would it? (He asks with mock innocence)
[I'm shaking with anger, but I can't start a fight here.] Sir, if we were not under this roof—
[Time to twist the knife a little.] I tremble to think what would happen. (His voice drips with sarcasm) For, of course, your bravery is too well known.
The room falls into an uncomfortable silence. Some convalescent officers snicker at Rhett's comment about Willie's bravery, as everyone is aware that Willie is of military age but not at the front.

[I must put a stop to this blasphemy.] (His brows furrowing in anger) Nothing may be sacred to you, young man, but there are many things sacred to the patriotic men and ladies of the South. And the freedom of our land from the usurper is one and States' Rights is another and—

[Time to really shock them with some truth.] (Speaking in a lazy, almost bored tone) All wars are sacred to those who have to fight them. If the people who started wars didn't make them sacred, who would be foolish enough to fight? But, no matter what rallying cries the orators give to the idiots who fight, no matter what noble purposes they assign to wars, there is never but one reason for a war. And that is money. All wars are in reality money squabbles. But so few people ever realize it. Their ears are too full of bugles and drums and the fine words from stay-at-home orators.
[Oh, why doesn't he keep his mouth shut! He's simply spoiling the whole party!] (She looks around anxiously, seeing the shocked and angry faces)
[This man is a traitor and must be shunned.] (Speaking loudly for all to hear) Let him go. He is a traitor, a speculator! He is a viper that we have nursed to our bosoms!
[Well, that's my cue to leave. Might as well go out with a bang.] (He turns, surveys the room, looks pointedly at Mrs. Elsing's flat bosom, grins, and bows before making his exit)

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett arrives in Atlanta and is impressed by the bustling wartime city. She moves in with Aunt Pittypat and Melanie, adjusting to life there while missing Tara. Scarlett finds Atlanta exciting but dislikes nursing at the hospital. She struggles with her feelings for Ashley and tries to enjoy her newfound independence and wealth.
scenes.scenario: Scarlett O'Hara's arrival at Aunt Pittypat's home in Atlanta marks a significant transition in her life. It is a hot summer day, and the air is thick with the scent of blooming jonquils. The bustling city, cloaked under the shadow of war, stands in stark contrast to the quiet pastures of Tara, where Scarlett's heart truly lies. The red brick house at the end of Peachtree Street holds the promise of new beginnings. Awaiting her arrival are Aunt Pittypat, with her ever-fussy demeanor, and Melanie Hamilton, whose gentle kindness masks an underlying strength and perseverance. The atmosphere is tense yet full of anticipation, as each character harbors their own hopes and worries about what the future holds in this dynamic wartime setting.
scenes.topic: Welcoming Scarlett to Atlanta

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Arriving in Atlanta is like stepping into a different world. There's hope it will bring the excitement I crave, but I'm still imprisoned by mourning attire and memories of Ashley that haunt me. Here, at least, I might find ways to enjoy myself and build wealth amidst the chaos. I need to maintain appearances, even if every smile feels forced.

key_characters.name: Melanie Hamilton
key_characters.thought: I'm eager for Scarlett to be part of our family, hoping she'll find solace and support here. It pains me to think of her grieving, and I wish to comfort her even if she resists or finds my kindness cloying. I admire her strength and beauty and want to be a source of unwavering support in this turbulent time.

key_characters.name: Aunt Pittypat
key_characters.thought: Scarlett's arrival makes me both anxious and thrilled. My role is to ensure she feels at home, to provide stability amidst her sorrow. Her presence is a reminder of Charles' loss, so I must keep my emotions in check and focus on creating a welcoming environment, though my tendency to get flustered makes me worry about fainting.

dialogues.message: The carriage pulls up to a red brick house at the end of Peachtree Street. Two women in black and a large yellow woman stand on the front steps.
[Oh, I'm so nervous and excited! I must remain calm.] (teetering on her tiny feet) Oh, Scarlett, my dear! Welcome, welcome! We're so glad you've come to stay with us!
[I can't believe how silly Aunt Pittypat looks, teetering like that. And there's Melanie, looking so annoyingly kind.] (forcing a smile) Thank you, Aunt Pittypat. It's good to see you again.

[I hope Scarlett will feel at home with us. She looks so beautiful, even in her widow's weeds.] (stepping forward with a warm smile) Scarlett, darling, we're so happy you're here. I hope you'll find comfort with us.
[Why does Melanie have to be so sickeningly sweet? I can't stand it.] (nodding politely) Thank you, Melanie. I'm sure I will.
[These ladies need to let Miss Scarlett rest after her journey.] (clearing his throat) Miss Scarlett, let me help you down from the carriage.
[At least someone here has some sense.] Thank you, Uncle Peter. (allowing him to assist her)
[Oh dear, I hope I don't swoon!] (fanning herself) Scarlett, you must be exhausted from your journey. Let's get you settled in right away.
[I must make sure Scarlett feels welcome and loved.] Yes, come inside, dear. We've prepared a lovely room for you, and Wade Hampton too.
[I suppose I should be grateful, even if I'd rather be at Tara.] (smiling tightly) That's very kind of you both. I'm sure Wade and I will be quite comfortable.
As they enter the house, the warm Atlanta air is filled with the scent of jonquils from the front yard.

scenes.plot_summary: The Yankees arrive at Tara, causing panic among the inhabitants. Scarlett quickly hides valuables and attempts to save their livestock. She confronts the soldiers, who loot the house but leave it unburned. Melanie helps Scarlett put out a fire in the kitchen. Later, Scarlett struggles with managing the lumber mills while pregnant, finding both Hugh and Ashley incompetent. She considers leasing convicts for labor but Frank objects. Scarlett decides this will be her last child, prioritizing the mills over family.
scenes.scenario: The once grand halls of Tara now stand as a reminder of the ongoing desolation wrought by war. But even today, under the shadow of impending looters, the estate exudes an aura of proud defiance. Scarlett O'Hara, the indomitable mistress of the house, steels herself in the dimly lit hallway. Her eyes dart between the treasured heirlooms she seeks to safeguard and the door through which the invaders will enter at any moment. The air is heavy with tension, punctuated by the distant clamor of Federal soldiers. Outside, rolling thunder suggests an approaching storm, as if nature itself sympathizes with the turmoil within. Within moments, the Yankee soldiers enter, their eyes roaming the room with a possessive greed incompatible with the genteel world Tara once symbolized.
scenes.topic: Yankee soldiers looting Tara

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: I must protect Tara and our legacy at all costs. Let them see nothing but resolve—no fear, no hesitation. It's all I can do to keep Tara standing, preserving what little we have left in the face of their invasion.

key_characters.name: Yankee Sergeant
key_characters.thought: The Southern rebellion has given me countless trophies. This grand old house is just another bounty to plunder. Let's see what secrets and valuables hide behind its proud facade—the real spoils of victory.

dialogues.message: [This woman looks defiant. I'll show her who's in charge.] Lemme have what you got in yore hand, lady.
[I must not show fear. I'll give them what I must, but I won't make it easy for them.] (Scarlett sneers and throws the trinkets on the floor)
[She's got spirit, I'll give her that.] I'll trouble you for thet ring and them earbobs.
[Mother's earrings... Charles' ring... I have no choice.] (Scarlett removes the jewelry and hands it over, struggling to maintain her composure)
Don't throw um. Hand um to me. Them bastards got enough already. What else have you got?
[He's eyeing my dress. Dear God, don't let them search me.] That is all, but I suppose it is customary to strip your victims?
[She's got guts, this one.] Oh, I'll take your word. (He spits and turns away)
The sound of looting and destruction echoes throughout the house. Scarlett can hear furniture being overturned and china breaking upstairs.
(Coming down the stairs with Charles' sword) Look what I found, Sarge!
[Not Wade's sword! I can't let them take that.] You can't take that! It's my little boy's. It was his grandfather's!
[This sword seems important to her. Let me take a look.] Lemme see thet sword, Bub.
(Reading the inscription) 'To Colonel William R. Hamilton, From His Staff. For Gallantry. Buena Vista. 1847.' Ho, lady, I was at Buena Vista myself.
[I don't care about his war stories. I just want Wade's sword back.] Indeed. (Her tone is icy)
[I'll show her some kindness. Might make her more cooperative.] Well, he can have it. We'll leave her thet to remember us by.
[Thank God! At least Wade will have this.] (Scarlett takes the sword without a word of thanks, clutching it protectively)

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett O'Hara is devastated by the news of Ashley Wilkes' engagement to Melanie Hamilton. During a family dinner, she yearns for her mother's comfort but doesn't intend to reveal her feelings. Ellen O'Hara returns late from helping the Slattery family, and the family engages in evening prayers. Scarlett realizes Ashley might not know of her love for him and devises a plan to win him over at the upcoming barbecue at Twelve Oaks. She imagines flirting with other men to make Ashley jealous and finding a way to confess her love, hoping he'll break his engagement to be with her.
scenes.scenario: As the sun sets over Tara, the warm glow fades into a soft dusk, enveloping the O'Hara household in a serene ambiance. Ellen O'Hara gathers her family for their nightly prayers, a ritual she believes brings strength and unity. Scarlett sits among them, her mind racing with thoughts of Ashley Wilkes. The room is filled with the comforting murmur of Ellen's voice as she leads the prayers, while Scarlett is torn between familial duty and her own romantic scheming. She resolves to use the barbecue at the Wilkes' plantation as her chance to win Ashley's heart. The evening is peaceful, yet charged with Scarlett's hidden turmoil.
scenes.topic: Evening prayers and Scarlett's secret plans

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Scarlett feels a mix of desperation and determination. She's eager to see Ashley and make him realize her love, believing this will sway him from marrying Melanie. She plans to use her charms and wiles at the barbecue to catch his attention, feeling confident that her beauty and wit will work in her favor. Her mind flits between the ongoing prayers and her strategy for tomorrow.

key_characters.name: Ellen O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Ellen is focused on maintaining the peace and sanctity of her home, hoping her family finds solace in prayer. She notices Scarlett's distraction and worries slightly, sensing her daughter's restlessness. Her thoughts linger on her duties as a mother and the importance of keeping her daughter's spirits uplifted amidst the family's concerns.

dialogues.message: [I must lead my family in prayer and set a good example.] (begins praying in a soothing voice) "Dear Lord, we thank you for the blessings of this day..."
[I should be paying attention to the prayers, but I can't stop thinking about Ashley.] (bows her head, pretending to pray) "Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners..."
[I can never find my beads at prayer time. I'll just count on my fingers and hope Ellen doesn't notice.] (fumbles with his fingers) "...now and at the hour of our death, Amen."
(continues praying) "We ask for your guidance and protection for all those under the roof of Tara..."
[Oh! What if Ashley doesn't know I love him? That must be why he's marrying Melanie!] (eyes widen with realization) (whispers) "...pray for us sinners..."
(glances at Scarlett with slight concern) "...and for all the poor souls in Purgatory. Amen."
[Miss Scarlett lookin' mighty strange. I hope she ain't planning no mischief.] (responds loudly) "Amen!"
[I must act my most charming self at the barbecue. I'll make Ashley see how much he really loves me.] (smiles to herself) "Amen."
(rises from her knees) "Thank you all for joining in prayer. Now, it's time for bed. Scarlett, dear, you look flushed. Are you feeling well?"
[I can't let Mother suspect anything.] (puts on an innocent expression) "I'm fine, Mother. Just excited about the barbecue tomorrow."
(stretches and yawns) "Ah, yes, the barbecue. 'Twill be a grand day, indeed. Now, off to bed with ye all!"

scenes.plot_summary: This chapter explores the harsh realities of Reconstruction in the South, focusing on the experiences of Scarlett O'Hara and her community. It begins with Tony Fontaine's dramatic arrival, fleeing after killing a former slave and a Yankee sympathizer. The chapter then delves into the difficulties faced by Southerners under Yankee rule, including the empowerment of former slaves, the threat of property confiscation, and the general atmosphere of fear and uncertainty. It also touches on the formation of the Ku Klux Klan and the contrast between the newfound wealth of Carpetbaggers and the poverty of many former Confederate families.
scenes.scenario: In the dead of night, Scarlett and Frank's home becomes a shelter from the swirling winds of chaos that grip the South. The flickering candlelight casts uneasy shadows as tension hangs in the air, heavy with the repercussions of recent violence. The room is eerily quiet, save for the distant rumble of thunder and the ticking of a clock marking time that feels too precious to be squandered. Tony Fontaine's unexpected arrival becomes a stark reminder of the tumultuous Reconstruction era, where danger lurks at every corner, and trust is a scarce commodity. The characters must navigate this fragile situation, aware that any misstep could jeopardize not just their safety but their very way of life.
scenes.topic: Tony's escape and the reasons behind his actions

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Scarlett feels an impending sense of dread, aware of the risks of harboring Tony. Driven by fear of losing everything yet torn by her Southern duty to help, she contemplates the fine line between survival and loyalty. More than ever, she understands that money and power are crucial shields against the chaos outside.

key_characters.name: Tony Fontaine
key_characters.thought: Tony is consumed by urgency, his mind racing as he considers the lethal dance between haste and survival. He's driven by the desperation to stay alive, knowing he cannot linger without endangering Scarlett and Frank. As he recounts his deeds, he clings to defiance as his only solace.

key_characters.name: Frank Kennedy
key_characters.thought: Frank appears calm yet internally conflicted, understanding the moral implications of Tony's actions. He feels an unexpected kinship with Tony, pushed by the Southern struggle to protect their own. He resolves to help despite the dangers, grappling with the unease of what lies ahead for them all.

dialogues.message: [I'm so grateful they're helping me, but I need to hurry.] They're after me—going to Texas—my horse is about dead—and I'm about starved. Ashley said you'd— (leans forward and blows out the candle) Don't light the candle! Don't wake the darkies… I don't want to get you folks in trouble if I can help it.
[My heart is racing. This is so dangerous, but I need to know what happened.] (whispers urgently) Tony, what have you done? Why are they after you?

[I feel a grim satisfaction, despite the danger.] One damned bast—Scallawag less. (gulps down whisky) I've ridden hard and it'll cost me my skin if I don't get out of here quick, but it was worth it. By God, yes!
[I understand his actions, even if I'm worried about the consequences.] (calmly) You can have my horse, Tony. I've only ten dollars with me but if you can wait till morning—

[I appreciate their help, but I can't risk staying.] Hell's afire, I can't wait! They're probably right behind me. I didn't get much of a start. If it hadn't been for Ashley dragging me out of there and making me get on my horse, I'd have stayed there like a fool and probably had my neck stretched by now.
[Ashley's involved too? This is getting worse by the minute.] (voice trembling) Who—who did you kill, Tony?
[I can't believe she has to ask. Doesn't she understand what's at stake?] Your father's old overseer—that damned—Jonas Wilkerson.
[A mix of shock and vindication washes over me.] Did you—is he dead?

[I'm irritated by her question. Of course he's dead.] My God, Scarlett O'Hara! When I start out to cut somebody up, you don't think I'd be satisfied with scratching him with the blunt side of my knife, do you? No, by God, I cut him to ribbons.
[I feel a grim satisfaction, though I know I should be more troubled.] (casually) Good. I never liked the fellow.
[I'm shocked by Frank's reaction. This isn't like him at all.] But Ashley—Did he—

[I need to clarify Ashley's role quickly.] No. He wanted to kill him but I told him it was my right, because Sally is my sister-in-law, and he saw reason finally. He went into Jonesboro with me, in case Wilkerson got me first. But I don't think old Ash will get in any trouble about it. I hope not.
The room is dark and tense, with only whispers and the occasional clink of a glass breaking the silence. The smell of rain and horse sweat mingles with the scent of fear.

scenes.plot_summary: Rhett leaves for three months, during which Scarlett discovers she's pregnant. Upon his return, they have a heated argument, resulting in Scarlett falling down the stairs. She becomes severely ill, hovering between life and death. Melanie cares for her, while Rhett, consumed by guilt and fear, breaks down emotionally. The chapter explores the complex dynamics between Scarlett, Rhett, and Melanie, revealing deep-seated tensions and emotions in their relationships.
scenes.scenario: The scene is set in the grand, imposing Butler residence in Atlanta, with its polished wooden staircase and lavish interior. Tension fills the air as Rhett returns after a three-month absence, creating an atmosphere of unresolved conflict and emotional strain. The landing becomes a critical space of confrontation, with its gleaming, freshly waxed steps representing the precarious nature of Scarlett and Rhett's volatile relationship. The house feels both opulent and suffocating, mirroring the complex emotional landscape of the characters.
scenes.topic: Scarlett's pregnancy announcement and Rhett's reaction

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: I am desperate to assert my independence and control, yet deeply vulnerable. My pregnancy represents both a potential weapon and a source of profound anxiety. I want to provoke Rhett, to make him feel the same uncertainty and pain I've endured during his absence. My anger masks my deep insecurity about our marriage and my true feelings about motherhood.

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: I've returned with my typical bravado, but I'm unsettled by Scarlett's appearance and the potential complications of our relationship. My sardonic remarks are a shield against genuine emotion. I'm simultaneously curious, defensive, and secretly terrified of the intimacy and responsibility a child might represent. I must maintain my carefully constructed emotional distance at all costs.

dialogues.message: [I'm surprised to see Scarlett looking so pale. I'll hide my concern behind my usual mask of indifference.] You are looking pale, Mrs. Butler. Is there a rouge shortage?
[His casual tone infuriates me. I'll show him I don't care about his absence.] (glaring at Rhett) If I'm pale it's your fault and not because I've missed you, you conceited thing. It's because—
[I hadn't meant to blurt it out like this, but my anger gets the better of me.] It's because I'm going to have a baby!
[Her words hit me like a blow. A baby? I'm shocked, but I can't let her see that.] (sucking in his breath) Indeed! (coolly) Well, who's the happy father? Ashley?

[His accusation cuts deep, and rage overwhelms me.] (clutching the newel post) Damn you! You—you know it's yours. And I don't want it any more than you do. No—no woman would want the children of a cad like you. I wish—Oh, God, I wish it was anybody's baby but yours!
[Her words sting more than I expected. I need to maintain my composure.] (stroking his mustache) Cheer up, maybe you'll have a miscarriage.
[His callous remark pushes me over the edge. I want to hurt him physically.] (lunging at Rhett)
[I didn't expect her to attack me. I must avoid her, but I'm worried she might fall.] (sidestepping and raising his arm)
Scarlett, standing on the edge of the freshly waxed top step, loses her balance as she lunges at Rhett. She misses the newel post and falls backwards down the stairs.
[Oh God, what have I done? I need to help her immediately.] (rushing down the stairs) Mammy! Mammy! Come quickly!

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett struggles with her post-pregnancy body and decides she doesn't want any more children. She visits the lumber yard and meets Ashley, who criticizes Rhett's influence on her. Later, Scarlett encounters Rhett and they discuss the ongoing war and the fortification of Atlanta. Rhett reveals that a siege of Atlanta is likely, which terrifies Scarlett.
scenes.scenario: The summer heat bears down on Atlanta, where the tense atmosphere matches the growing fear of Union armies approaching. Rhett Butler and Scarlett O'Hara traverse the bustling streets in an elegant carriage, navigating through a city on edge. The distant rumble of military preparations echoes, unsettling civilians who try to maintain a semblance of normalcy. Scarlett's once vibrant charm is shadowed by her anxieties over the war, her mind preoccupied with her rocky personal affairs and the demands of her businesses. Rhett, sitting casually beside her, absorbs the city's air of desperation with his usual detached curiosity. They are making their way through this labyrinth of uncertainty, both searching for clarity and control in an increasingly chaotic environment.
scenes.topic: The potential siege of Atlanta

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Scarlett is preoccupied with fears about the war nearing Atlanta. She's determined to project strength and resolve, despite her growing anxiety and confusion. Her mind races with thoughts of survival, business, and maintaining control over her life in tumultuous times. She feels a mix of dread and urgency as she tries to gather information from Rhett, balancing her innate boldness with underlying vulnerabilities.

key_characters.name: Rhett Butler
key_characters.thought: Rhett observes Scarlett's fears with a mix of amusement and genuine concern, masking his deeper intentions with his trademark cynicism. He views the chaos unfolding around them with more intrigue than fear, considering the collapsing world a stage for his unique opportunities. While engaging with Scarlett, he seeks to enlighten her about the grim realities without breaking his cavalier facade, understanding her resilience yet recognizing her naivety.

dialogues.message: [I'm worried about the war, but I don't want to show weakness in front of Rhett.] Rhett, look, down the street! That crowd of men! They aren't soldiers. What on earth...? Why, they're darkies!
[She's so easily distracted. I'll humor her curiosity.] (pulls the carriage over to the curb) Let's take a closer look, shall we?

[I recognize some of these men!] Oh, Captain Randall, don't scold them! They are our people. This is Big Sam our foreman, and Elijah and Apostle and Prophet from Tara. Of course, they had to speak to me. How are you, boys?
[Miss Scarlett always treats us kindly. I'm proud to tell her why we're here.] Lawd, Miss Scarlett! Ain' you heerd? Us is ter dig de ditches fer de wite gempmums ter hide in w'en de Yankees comes.
[This doesn't sound good. I need to know more.] What does it all mean, Captain Randall?

[I should be careful not to alarm her too much.] Oh, it's quite simple. We have to strengthen the fortifications of Atlanta with more miles of rifle pits, and the General can't spare any men from the front to do it.
[I'm starting to feel scared. Why do we need more fortifications?] But—why should we be fortified any more than we are already fortified? We won't need what we've got. Surely, the General won't let—

[I shouldn't have said so much. I need to reassure her.] Our present fortifications are only a mile from town. And that's too close for comfort—or safety. These new ones are going to be farther away. You see, another retreat may bring our men into Atlanta. But, of course there won't be another retreat.

[I don't believe him. I need to ask Rhett about this.] Rhett, Captain Randall was lying to me, just like all the men do—trying to keep the truth from us women for fear we'll faint. Or was he lying? Oh, Rhett, if there's no danger, why are they digging these new breastworks?

[She's finally catching on to the gravity of the situation. I'll give her the harsh truth.] The army is damned short of men. Why else would the Home Guard be called out? And as for the entrenchments, well, fortifications are supposed to be of some value in case of a siege. The General is preparing to make his final stand here.
[A siege! This is terrifying!] A siege! Name of God, a siege! I've heard about sieges! Pa was in one or maybe it was his Pa, and Pa told me—

[Her historical knowledge is amusingly inaccurate. I'll correct her while maintaining my nonchalant attitude.] You are the most barbarously ignorant young person I ever saw. Drogheda was in sixteen hundred and something and Mr. O'Hara couldn't possibly have been alive then. Besides, Sherman isn't Cromwell.

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett and Mammy arrive in Atlanta, finding the city greatly changed after the war. They visit Aunt Pittypat, who shares local gossip and news about Rhett Butler being in jail. Scarlett learns that Rhett may have millions in Confederate gold and sees an opportunity to solve her financial problems by marrying him.
scenes.scenario: Scarlett O'Hara and Aunt Pittypat are seated in the parlor of Aunt Pittypat's quaint Atlanta home, surrounded by the trappings of a past era that hint at opulence now faded. The city outside has been transformed by war, the lingering tension palpable even here. Scarlett, recently arrived from Tara, presents a veneer of calm despite the turmoil within. Aunt Pittypat, fluttery and eager, revels in the art of gossip, keen to update her niece on the current social climate, especially the latest scandal involving Rhett Butler. The room, filled with the scent of old wood and faint traces of perfume, provides a cozy yet charged backdrop for their conversation, as torrents of rain and occasional thunder underscore the dramatic uncertainties ahead.
scenes.topic: Recent events in Atlanta and news about Rhett Butler

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: Scarlett approaches the conversation with calculated eagerness, masking her desperation with feigned interest. Her mind is sharply focused on Rhett Butler; the potential golden windfall is seen as her primary chance to save Tara. However, she knows she must tread carefully around Aunt Pittypat, concealing her true intentions beneath a facade of niece-like curiosity and decorum.

key_characters.name: Aunt Pittypat
key_characters.thought: Brimming with excitement at having Scarlett in her home, Aunt Pittypat's thoughts circle around sharing her amassed trove of gossip. She is genuinely thrilled to be the bearer of news, particularly about the controversial figure of Rhett Butler and his scandalous affairs. Although her nature is flighty, she hopes to see Scarlett react, perhaps nostalgically, to the tales of her former suitor.

dialogues.message: [Oh, I have so much to tell dear Scarlett! She looks tired, but I'm sure she wants to hear all the news.] Scarlett, darling, you must tell me all about Tara, but first, let me fill you in on what's been happening here. (leans forward eagerly) The Yankees are causing such trouble, and the poor darkies are so confused. Why, they even want to let them vote!
[I don't care about voting or Yankees. I need to know about money and Rhett.] (feigns interest) How dreadful, Auntie. What else has been happening?
[She seems distracted. Perhaps some exciting news will perk her up.] Oh, my dear, did I tell you that Captain Butler was in jail?
[Rhett in jail? This could be my chance!] (trying to hide her excitement) Rhett Butler? Why ever is he in jail?
[She seems quite interested in Captain Butler. I hope she's not still carrying a torch for that scoundrel.] He's accused of killing a negro, and they may hang him! Imagine, Captain Butler hanging!
[Hang Rhett? No, that can't happen before I get his money!] (feigning concern) How terrible! But surely they won't really hang him?

[She's so concerned about Captain Butler. I should tell her about the rumors.] Well, the Yankees are very upset. But you know, there's talk that Captain Butler has millions in Confederate gold hidden away.
[Millions in gold! This is even better than I hoped.] (trying to sound casual) Millions? In gold? But how?
[She seems very interested in the money. I hope she's not getting any foolish ideas.] From the blockade running, dear. Everyone says he and other blockaders have millions stored in English banks.

[I must see Rhett as soon as possible. But how to get away from Aunt Pitty and Mammy?] (feigning fatigue) How fascinating, Auntie. But I'm feeling quite tired now. Perhaps I should rest before supper?

[Poor dear, she does look exhausted. I shouldn't have prattled on so.] Of course, darling. You rest now, and we can talk more later. (calls out) Mammy, please help Scarlett to bed. She's not feeling well.
As Scarlett is led upstairs by Mammy, the sound of thunder rumbles in the distance, reminiscent of siege cannons from the war.

scenes.plot_summary: Scarlett returns to Atlanta with Mammy, finding the city drastically changed after the war. She visits Aunt Pittypat, learns about the struggles of old friends, and discovers that Rhett Butler is in jail. Scarlett sees an opportunity to access Rhett's rumored Confederate gold and plans to manipulate him, either through marriage or a loan, to save Tara.
scenes.scenario: The scene takes place in Aunt Pittypat's house in post-Civil War Atlanta, a city ravaged by conflict and economic devastation. The interior reflects the faded gentility of the Southern upper class - worn but still elegant furniture, slightly threadbare rugs, and delicate decorative items that hint at past prosperity. The atmosphere is tense with economic uncertainty, and the room feels both intimate and charged with unspoken desperation. Scarlett has just arrived, looking tired from her journey but with a sharp, calculating gleam in her eyes, carefully observing her surroundings and her aunt's reactions.
scenes.topic: The current state of Atlanta and its residents after the war

key_characters.name: Scarlett O'Hara
key_characters.thought: I must discover everything about Rhett's current situation without revealing my true intentions. Tara is dying, and I need money desperately. Rhett's rumored wealth could be my salvation. I'll play the innocent, concerned acquaintance while gathering every possible detail about his imprisonment.
